newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian king condemns shooting of journalist.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian king condemns shooting of journalist.

text.p: King Norodom Sihanouk on Saturday strongly condemned Thursday's shooting of a young Cambodian newspaper editor, stating the incident threatened the country's democracy and tarnished its reputation.
Late on Thursday, 26-year-old Leng Samnang was shot in the stomach by an unidentified gunman in an attack his colleagues suggested was politically motivated.
The attack occurred as the newspaper editor was driving home from a birthday party for co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh of the royalist FUNCINPEC party.

Seven uniformed men carrying AK-47s and dressed like military or bodyguards, surrounded the editor, who was beaten and shot, said Cheng Sokna, the publisher of Leng Samnang's newspaper Kmunith Kaun Khmer.

"This act follows many previous terrible crimes in our capital, which worsens the democratic, multi-party system and the reputation of Cambodia in the international arena, breaking down our national society with no medicine to treat its sicknesses," Sihanouk wrote in a statement.

The attack came after repeated threats to Kumnith Kaun Khmer, or "Idea of Cambodia's Children", said Cheng Sokna, who said his paper takes a highly critical stance against co-Premier Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP).
It also followed reports of threats to several other newspapers and the unsolved murders of three Cambodian journalists in the past two years.
Sihanouk bemoaned Cambodia's lawlessness and appealed for an end to the violence.
"I would like to appeal to my compatriots again to stop any unlawful acts that threaten national peace and harmony," he wrote.
Leng Samnang's brother, Leng Thy, told Reuters on Saturday that the editor's condition remained stable and that he was able to speak a little.
CPP officials have strongly denied any intimidation of journalists, including those at Leng Samnang's newspaper, which is aligned with the royalist FUNCINPEC party.
They suggested a personal dispute, rather than political motivations, was behind the attack.
Chief of penal police Mok Chito, a member of CPP, said a dispute with neighbours over Leng Samnang urinating on their property, may have been the cause of the attack.
A CPP newspaper editor alleged Leng Samnang was drunk and nearly ran over the gunman, leading to the shooting.

"This was not caused by a personal problem," said Leng Thy, who said his brother suspected he was being followed in recent days. But Leng Thy declined to speculate on who might be responsible for a political attack.
